name: Nanogen hair fibres

lead: Nanogen Hair Thickening Fibres are small keratin fibres, described by the brand and retailers as 100% keratin and made in the UK, that cling to existing hair by static charge. Dusted over thinning areas, they thicken the look of each strand and reduce the visible gaps where scalp shows through, giving fuller-looking hair for the day.

They are one of several hair building fibre products sold as a concealer for thinning hair. The effect is cosmetic and temporary: the fibres do not alter hair growth, and they come out with shampooing. Retail reviews are mixed, with some buyers saying the result lasts the day and others reporting it loosens within minutes or hours.

paras: Users style their hair first, using their own hair to cover as much scalp as possible, then shake small amounts of fibre over the thinning area and blend with the fingers. For mixed shades the brand suggests using the darker colour as a base and the lighter on top. A separate locking spray, held about 10 cm away and sprayed several times, is offered by the brand for hold in wind and rain. The fibres are removed by shampooing.

No serious harms have been reported for the product. The product is for external use, the label advice is to avoid contact with the eyes and stop use if irritation occurs, and retailers suggest checking with a pharmacist or doctor if there is a scalp condition. Because the fibres sit on the surface, they can transfer to pillows, hats or hands, and wetness or wind can disturb them.

chain: Keratin fibres cling to existing hair by static
Strands look thicker and scalp is less visible
Fuller-looking hairline and crown until the next wash
angle.text: The fibres give the look of thicker hair in minutes by covering visible scalp. The effect is cosmetic, tied to the colour match and to how well the fibres stay on.

lead: Nanogen Hair Thickening Fibres are a cosmetic hair concealer made by the UK brand Nanogen. The brand describes them as 100% keratin fibres made in the UK, sold in several shades and in 15 g and 30 g sizes.[1] When sprinkled onto thinning hair, the electrostatically charged fibres attach to existing strands and visually thicken them, so thinning areas look denser.

People use them to disguise hair loss at the crown, temples and parting line without treatment or surgery. The look is immediate, and the fibres wash out at the next shampoo.[1] The brand also sells a Fibre Locking Spray for water resistance and shampoos for removal.[1]
No clinical trials of Nanogen fibres have been published. Retailer reviews are mixed on how long the effect lasts.

paras: The product is a fine powder of coloured fibres. Retailers describe them as made of natural keratin, the protein hair is made of, with an electrostatic charge that helps them cling to hair strands. Shades listed by retailers include black, dark brown, medium brown, light brown, grey and white.

According to the brand's application page, users dry and style their hair, shake the fibres over the thinning area at a slight angle, blend with the fingers and optionally set with a locking spray; the page recommends the darker colour first for mixed shades and says the fibres wash out with shampoo.[1] Fibre products come up on T Nation forum threads about hair loss.[2][3][4]
No studies found. The fibres are a cosmetic and have not been the subject of published clinical trials.

The brand's page does not address safety in its instructions and links to a separate medical disclaimer.[1] Retail listings state the product is for external use, advise avoiding the eyes and stopping use if irritation occurs, and recommend checking with a pharmacist or doctor for scalp conditions. Customer reviews quoted by retailers vary: one says the effect lasted around 20 minutes, another says the product does what it claims.
